voices.FATHER: He speaks in a deep, slow, resonant old man's voice with a neutral General American accent, warm and grandfatherly, with measured broadcast pacing.
voices.IDA: She speaks in a young woman's low, soft, tired voice with a neutral General American accent.
voices.NANA: She speaks in an old woman's gentle, slightly thin, warm voice with a neutral General American accent.

style: Flat 2D cel-painted animation style; keep the exact character design, colours and line work of the first frame.

jobs.prompt: Television broadcast. The elderly man sits perfectly composed and speaks directly into the lens, warm and slow: "Good evening, my children. The harvest is in. The sea is calm." Minimal head movement, an almost unnaturally smooth stillness, one slow blink. Locked-off camera, very slow push-in. Soft studio room tone, no music.

Close-up television broadcast. The old man, calm and kind, says "I am well." Then, after a small pause, gently: "Eat something warm before you sleep." Very little movement besides his mouth and one blink. Locked-off camera, slow push-in. Soft studio room tone, no music.

Television broadcast, one continuous take. The elderly man sits composed and speaks directly into the lens, slowly, with long pauses between lines, his calm slowly giving way to quiet tenderness: "Good evening, my children." (pause) "I died in the spring." (pause) "I'm sorry I stayed so long." (pause) "Tomorrow, you'll have to talk to each other." (pause) "Eat something warm before you sleep." After the last line he holds the lens for a moment, then slowly closes his eyes and stays still with his eyes closed. Locked-off camera with a very slow continuous push-in from medium close-up to close-up. Soft studio room tone, no music.

Close-up of Ida lit from below by cold cyan screen light, staring at the screen with quiet defiance. She says flatly, almost to herself: "No, you're not." Her jaw tightens after the line. Static camera. Quiet hall hum, no music.

Medium close-up: Ida at her desk, turned away from her monitors, holds a small phone to her ear and speaks softly, eyes lowered: "Nana. Don't wait up tonight." Slight head movement, a tired breath. Static camera, slight push-in. Quiet hall hum, no music.

Close-up: an elderly woman holds an old telephone handset to her ear, her face half in warm lamplight and half in the blue glow of a television. Lightly, with a small smile: "I always wait up. He's on soon." Her eyes drift toward the television. Static camera. Rain on the window, a clock ticking, no music.

Close-up: Ida, phone at her ear, lifts her eyes toward the off-screen monitors and asks, hesitantly: "Why do you still watch him?" She swallows after the line. Static camera. Quiet hall hum, no music.

Close-up: the elderly woman, handset at her ear and eyes on the blue television, smiles to herself and says simply: "For the ending." A pause, then warmly: "Eat something warm, love." Static camera. Rain on the window, a clock ticking, no music.

Close-up: Ida raises a small phone to her ear, stunned, eyes glistening. In the blurred foreground a red desk telephone keeps ringing. She starts to say "Nana—" and stops, breath catching. Static camera. A red telephone bell in a silent hall, no music.

Close-up: an elderly woman lit only by a warm lamp holds an old telephone handset to her ear; the television behind her is dark. Calm and tender, she says: "I know, love." A small smile. Static camera. Rain on the window, a clock ticking, no music.
Close-up: Ida, phone at her ear, barely able to speak, asks: "How long?" Her lips tremble; her eyes fill. Static camera. The silence of a vast hall, no music.

Close-up: the elderly woman, lamp-lit, handset at her ear, amused and tender, answers: "Since he started telling me to eat." A soft laugh in her eyes; she tilts her head slightly. Then, after a pause, softly and warmly: "Come home. The soup's still warm." Static camera. Rain, a clock ticking, no music.

Ida sits at her desk, lit cold cyan by a monitor just off-frame left, and makes two small precise corrections with a stylus, eyes narrowed with concentration, then exhales. Her lips stay closed. Static camera, very slight push-in. Dust drifting in the light.

Low angle from behind a lone woman standing at her desk in a vast dark hall, looking up at an enormous wall of glowing screens. She is completely still; only her scarf stirs slightly and dust drifts through the cold light beams. Slow, steady, accelerating push-in toward the screens.

Extreme close-up of Ida's eyes, wet, reflecting cold cyan light. A tear gathers on the lower lid; she blinks once, slowly, and keeps staring forward, unflinching. Her mouth is not visible. Static camera.

Ida sits at her lone desk in a vast dark hall, looking up at a giant screen above the camera. Her face is lit cold cyan and her eyes are wet; she does not move and her lips stay closed while she listens. Slow pull-back revealing the empty covered desks around her. Dust drifting in the light.

Close-up: an elderly woman holds a steaming teacup near her chin, facing a television off-screen, her face lit by its cold blue light, warm lamplight behind her. She listens without speaking, lips closed; her eyes glisten and the corners of her mouth lift into a small, knowing smile. Steam curls from the cup. Static camera.

Close-up: Ida, a small phone at her ear, eyes closed, listening. A tear runs down her cheek and a quiet laugh breaks through her crying, her shoulders shaking slightly; she does not speak. Static camera, slow push-in.
